nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of Fe-Ni(OH)₂/NF
nodes.procedure: NF pieces were cleaned and immersed in a solution containing HCl and FeCl₃, then subjected to hydrothermal treatment. The HCl etches the NF surface forming Ni²⁺ ions. Once HCl is consumed, Ni²⁺ ions co-precipitate in situ with Fe³⁺ ions to form single-crystalline Fe-Ni(OH)₂ nanoflake arrays on NF (following dissolution-precipitation mechanism per Tian et al.).

nodes.source_text: As illustrated in Fig. 1a, single-crystalline Fe-Ni(OH)₂/NF nanoflake arrays were grown on NF by a simple hydrothermal method using NF as both the substrate and Ni source... HCl etches the NF surface, forming Ni²⁺ ions. Once the HCl is consumed, the generated Ni²⁺ ions co-precipitate in situ with the Fe³⁺ ions

nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of Ni(OH)₂/NF
nodes.procedure: Single-crystalline Ni(OH)₂ nanoflake arrays on NF were fabricated using the same hydrothermal procedure as Fe-Ni(OH)₂/NF, but in the absence of FeCl₃. NF pieces were cleaned and immersed in HCl solution, then hydrothermally treated following dissolution-precipitation mechanism where HCl etches NF surface forming Ni²⁺ ions which precipitate as Ni(OH)₂ nanoflakes.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns indexed to hexagonal Ni(OH)2 (JCPDS 03-0177) and cubic Ni (JCPDS 04-0850), showing no significant influence of Fe on crystal structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of Fe-Ni(OH)2/NF and Ni(OH)2/NF (Fig. S1) are almost identical, and can be indexed to hexagonal Ni(OH)2 (JCPDS Card No. 03-0177) and cubic Ni (JCPDS Card No. 04-0850).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows NF surface completely covered with vertically-aligned Fe-Ni(OH)2 nanoflake arrays.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1b, the surface of the NF is completely covered with vertically-aligned Fe-Ni(OH)2 nanoflake arrays.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows Fe-Ni(OH)2 nanoflake is perfect single crystal with hexagonal phase, 120° dihedral angle, hexagonal side length ~1.5 μm, thickness ~100 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Close observation by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) shows that the Fe-Ni(OH)2 nanoflake is a perfect single crystal with a hexagonal phase... hexagonal side length of the Fe-Ni(OH)2 nanoflakes is about 1.5 μm, while the thickness is about 100 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern confirms hexagonal phase of single-crystalline Fe-Ni(OH)2 nanoflake.
nodes.evidence_snippet: demonstrated by the 120° dihedral angle and corresponding selected area electron diffraction (SAED) spots (Fig. 1c).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringes with 0.27 nm interplanar spacing corresponding to (100) and (010) planes of hexagonal Ni(OH)2, no crystal defects observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Fig. 1d, the distinct and consecutive lattice fringes with an interplanar spacing of 0.27 nm correspond well to the d-spacing of (100) and (010) planes of hexagonal Ni(OH)2. No obvious crystal defects can be observed.

properties.description: High-resolution TEM image with lattice fringes

nodes.characterization_summary: FFT pattern consistent with SAED, confirming single crystalline nature of Fe-Ni(OH)2 nanoflake.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding fast Fourier transform (FFT) pattern is consistent with the SAED result, further confirming the single crystalline nature of the resultant Fe-Ni(OH)2 nanoflake.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and EDS show uniform distribution of O, Fe, and Ni throughout Fe-Ni(OH)2 nanoflake.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) and energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) elemental analysis reveal the presence of O, Fe, and Ni, as well as their uniform distribution throughout the Fe-Ni(OH)2 nanoflake.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS confirms presence of O, Fe, and Ni with uniform distribution in Fe-Ni(OH)2 nanoflake.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) and energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) elemental analysis reveal the presence of O, Fe, and Ni, as well as their uniform distribution throughout the Fe-Ni(OH)2 nanoflake.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows surface composition O (74.64 at.%), Fe (22.72 at.%), Ni (2.64 at.%); Fe 2p3/2 at 712.5 eV, 2p1/2 at 724.6 eV (Fe3+); Ni 2p peaks shift +0.4 eV indicating electron transfer Ni→Fe; O 1s peaks at 529.1 eV (Fe-O), 530.4 eV (Ni-O), 532.1 eV (adsorbed water).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Quantitative analysis indicates that the surface composition of O, Fe, and Ni is 74.64, 22.72, and 2.64 at. %, respectively... Fe 2p3/2 (712.5 eV) and Fe 2p1/2 (724.6 eV)... the Ni 2p3/2 and Ni 2p1/2 peaks in Fe-Ni(OH)2/NF shift to a higher binding energy by ~0.4 eV... In the O 1s region... peaks located at 529.1, 530.4, and 532.1 eV can be assigned to Fe-O, Ni-O, and adsorbed water, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV in 0.85-0.9 V vs RHE determines Cdl = 712 μF cm⁻² (Rf = 11.87) for Fe-Ni(OH)2/NF, 757 μF cm⁻² (Rf = 12.62) for Ni(OH)2/NF vs 60 μF cm⁻² smooth surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the double-layer capacitance (Cdl) of Fe-Ni(OH)2/NF, Ni(OH)2/NF, and NF electrode was determined by CV measurements... in the potential window of 0.85-0.9 V vs. RHE... average Cdl calculated... is 712, 757, and 453.6 μF cm⁻²... Given that a smooth electrode surface has a Cdl of 60 μF cm⁻², the relative roughness factor (Rf)... 11.87, 12.62, and 7.56.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows Fe-Ni(OH)2/NF has smallest charge transfer resistance Rct among samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the electrochemical impedance spectra of the various samples, Fe-Ni(OH)2/NF shows the smallest charge transfer resistance (Rct, Fig. 2d).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS detects no Ni or Fe ions (<1 ppb) in electrolyte after long-term stability test, indicating extraordinary chemical stability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: no signals for Ni²⁺/Ni³⁺ and Fe³⁺ were detected throughout the whole test, that is, the concentration of both Ni and Fe ions was below the detection limit of ICP-MS (< 1 ppb).

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER SEM shows well-aligned Fe-Ni(OH)2 nanoflake arrays well preserved, indicating strong structural durability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: as shown in the SEM images of Fe-Ni(OH)2/NF after long-term OER electrolysis (Fig. S9), the well-aligned nanoflake arrays were well preserved.
